fields.name: Display name
fields.syncIntervalHint: How often filex walks this storage for changes made outside it (poll mode). Leave empty for the server default (15 minutes). A large, rarely changing storage is happier with a long interval; a scan that outlasts its interval is not started twice.
fields.rbacHint: When on, non-admins see only the files and folders granted to them (listed under Folder access). When off, everyone opens the storage according to their role.
fields.followSymlinks: Follow symlinks that leave this folder
fields.nameChangedWarning: Clients address this storage by name. Renaming it changes the WebDAV, SFTP, S3 and NFS paths - a mount or bookmark using the old name will start answering 404 until you update it.
fields.stableAddressHint: Mounts and scripts can use this instead of the name. It is assigned once and never changes, so renaming the storage does not break them.

fieldHelp.path: Directory on the server. It is created if missing; filex never mounts /.
fieldHelp.followSymlinks: A symlink pointing INSIDE this folder is always followed. This governs only links pointing outside it: off, they are listed with a badge saying why they will not open, and cannot be opened, written to or deleted through; on, filex treats the linked files as part of the storage - including for indexing, virus scanning, quota and deletion.
fieldHelp.scanExclude: One pattern per line, relative to the storage root: * matches within a name, ** any number of folders, and a pattern without a / matches that name at any depth (.* skips every hidden file and folder). The scan does not go into a matching folder, and matching files are not catalogued, indexed, thumbnailed or virus-scanned. This saves work; it is not access control - the files stay on the storage, reachable by path, over WebDAV/SFTP and through the AI tools. Anything catalogued before you add a pattern stays as it is.
fieldHelp.lazyFill: Click first, fill in the background: the folder somebody opens is cataloged first, and a slow background pass catalogs the rest, so search, folder sizes and usage end up covering the whole storage. Only on open: nothing runs in the background. Only the folders people open are cataloged, and search, folder sizes and usage say that they cover those folders only. Sync now catalogs everything once.
fieldHelp.lazyMaxWatches: Folders people open are watched for changes made outside filex. Past this many, the folder opened longest ago stops being watched and is checked again the next time somebody opens it.
fieldHelp.lazyWatchTTL: A folder nobody has opened for this long stops being watched. It is checked again the next time somebody opens it.
fieldHelp.prefix: Sub-folder inside the bucket. Required: filex never takes ownership of the bucket root.
fieldHelp.root: Sub-folder on the backend. Required: filex never mounts the account root.
fieldHelp.endpoint: Leave empty for AWS S3. Any S3-compatible store needs its endpoint.
fieldHelp.pathStyle: On for every non-AWS store. It is turned on automatically when an endpoint is set and this was never touched.
fieldHelp.disablePresign: On by default: uploads and the downloads behind public share links stream through filex, so the bucket endpoint never has to be reachable from a browser (a LAN-only MinIO just works). Turn it off only when the endpoint is reachable from your users' browsers (AWS, a public MinIO) and you want them to talk to the bucket directly - faster for very large files, and the store must accept SDK-signed URLs (Ceph RGW / some Hetzner setups answer SignatureDoesNotMatch).
fieldHelp.sftpAuth: Either a password or a private key is required.
fieldHelp.keyPath: Path to a key file on the server, read when the storage starts. Used when the PEM field is empty.
fieldHelp.knownHosts: OpenSSH known_hosts path for strict host-key checking. Default is trust-on-first-use in ~/.filex/known_hosts.
fieldHelp.hostKey: A single public key in authorized_keys / known_hosts line form.
fieldHelp.insecureSkipHostKey: Accepts any host key. Only for throwaway hosts.
fieldHelp.tls: Plain FTP sends credentials in the clear - turn this on whenever the server supports it.
fieldHelp.passive: Off switches to active mode, which needs the server to dial back into this host.
fieldHelp.smbShare: The share name alone, without the server: `media`, not `\\nas\media`.
fieldHelp.smbDomain: Only for a Windows domain account. Leave empty for a NAS.
fieldHelp.smbRoot: Sub-folder inside the share. Leave empty for the whole share.
fieldHelp.s3AttemptTimeout: How long one attempt may wait for a sign of life from the store: connecting, the TLS handshake, the answer after the request is sent, and each next piece of the answer. A transfer that keeps moving is never cut, however long it takes; an upload the store stops taking is cut after 60 seconds, or after this if it is longer. Copies and renames wait up to 10 minutes for the answer, because the store answers them only when the copy is done.
fieldHelp.s3MaxAttempts: How many times a request is tried in all when the failure can pass: a network error, a timeout, a 5xx answer, throttling. 1 turns retrying off. A refusal (403, a missing bucket, a host name that does not resolve) is never retried.
fieldHelp.s3TotalTimeout: No new attempt starts unless it could finish within this many seconds of the first, so an upload or a listing on a store that is down reports the outage within this time. A transfer that is under way is not cut. A request that timed out is tried again only when this is at least twice the attempt timeout.
fieldHelp.attemptTimeout: How long one attempt may wait for a sign of life from the server: connecting, logging in, the answer to each request, and each next piece of a transfer. A transfer that keeps moving is never cut, however long it takes; an upload the server stops taking is cut after 60 seconds, or after this if it is longer.
fieldHelp.webdavAttemptTimeout: How long one attempt may wait for a sign of life from the server: connecting, logging in, the answer to each request, and each next piece of a transfer. A transfer that keeps moving is never cut, however long it takes; an upload the server stops taking is cut after 60 seconds, or after this if it is longer. Copies, moves and deletes wait up to 10 minutes for the answer, because the server answers them only when the work is done.
fieldHelp.maxAttempts: How many times a request is tried in all when the failure can pass: the connection is refused or drops, no answer comes in time, the server answers that it is unavailable (5xx). 1 turns retrying off. A refusal (a wrong password, a missing folder, a certificate that does not verify) is never retried, and neither is an upload that has started sending.
fieldHelp.totalTimeout: No new attempt starts unless it could finish within this many seconds of the first, so a server that is down is reported within this time. A transfer that is under way is not cut. A request that timed out is tried again only when this is at least twice the attempt timeout.

threeAddresses.title: Three machines, three addresses
threeAddresses.browser: Your browser loads the editor's JavaScript straight from the document server URL below, so that address has to work in a browser - not only inside the container network.
threeAddresses.server: The filex process fetches the document server's health endpoint from the same URL. This is what the Test button checks.
threeAddresses.callback: The document server fetches the document from filex and posts the save back to filex's public URL, so that address has to work from inside the document server's container:
threeAddresses.diagnose: When something fails, these two commands say which half is wrong:
threeAddresses.fromWorkstation: from a workstation - the browser leg
threeAddresses.fromDocumentServer: from inside the document server container - the callback leg

legs.callback: From the document server back to filex:
legs.cannotCheck: not checked - filex cannot make the document server issue a request on demand. The warnings below are the shapes that certainly cannot work.
legs.disagree: filex reaches this address and your browser does not. That is what a container-internal name looks like: the editor loads in the browser, so it will fail there.
legs.callbackOk: reached filex - the document server downloaded a test file through the same signed address a document uses
legs.callbackBad: did NOT reach filex. The document opens and the save never comes back.
legs.callbackUnchecked: could not be measured; the warnings below are the shapes that certainly cannot work.

browserStates.wrongContent: something answered, but it is not this service
browserStates.timeout: timed out - nothing answered and nothing refused
browserStates.mixedContent: blocked: this admin page is HTTPS and that address is HTTP

advisories.browser_bare_host: “{host}” is a single-label host name. filex can reach it from inside the container network, but your browser loads this service directly and cannot resolve it. Use an address a browser can open.
advisories.browser_loopback_host: This is a loopback address, but filex is published at {publicUrl} - the people who open it are not on this host, and to their browser “{host}” means their own machine.
advisories.public_url_loopback: The document server fetches the document from filex and posts the save back to {publicUrl}. Inside its own container that address is the document server, not filex.
advisories.public_url_bare_host: filex's public URL ({publicUrl}) is a container-network name. The document server can reach it, but share links and emails built from it will not open in a browser outside that network.
advisories.public_url_unresolved: filex itself cannot resolve “{host}”. That is expected if your document server uses a different DNS view; otherwise the public URL points at a name nothing can look up.
advisories.jwt_not_enforced: The document server accepted an unsigned request, so JWT is off on it. It still checks the token in filex's editor configuration, with its own secret, and refuses it, so documents do not open ("The document security token is not correctly formed"); it refuses to download from private addresses; and it sends its save callbacks unsigned, which filex refuses. Set JWT_ENABLED=true and JWT_SECRET to the same secret on the document server.

noSecret.title: ONLYOFFICE has no JWT secret
noSecret.body: Without a secret, filex cannot tell a genuine save from a forged one: anyone who can reach its save address could overwrite your files. That is why filex does not open or save documents with ONLYOFFICE until a secret is set. Enter the same secret as the document server's {env}.

fieldHints.max_concurrent: A whole number from 1 to 64; more at once are asked to try again.
fieldHints.email_domain: With corp.example, the account alex signs in as alex{'@'}corp.example. Empty: the address this installation chose for operating-system accounts. Choose it before the first sign-in.
fieldHints.ca_pem: The private CA the directory's certificate is signed by, pasted as it is. Empty: the system's trusted roots.
fieldHints.show_refusal_reason: Off by default. On, a person whose password was right but who still may not sign in here (no account is opened at a first sign-in, or they are in no allowed group) is told why. The sign-in form then also tells anybody who is guessing that a password is right - a password that may open other services that use the same accounts.
fieldHints.trust_email: Off by default. Off, an address the provider does not mark verified (email_verified) opens no existing account that is not yet bound to an SSO identity, and a new account for it is opened switched off until an administrator approves it. Turn it on only for a provider whose addresses all belong to the people who hold them: anybody who can set an address there can then sign in to the account with that address.
fieldHints.user_filter: Finds the person signing in. Every %s is the name they typed.
fieldHints.group_attr: The attribute on a person that lists their groups. Active Directory and lldap: memberOf.
fieldHints.group_filter: Only when people don’t carry their groups: finds them by a search instead. %s is the person’s DN, %u the name they signed in with - e.g. (member=%s).
fieldHints.group_base_dn: Where groups are searched for. Empty: the base DN.
fieldHints.sync_interval: How often sync runs on its own - e.g. 6h, at least 5m. Empty: only when you press Sync now.
fieldHints.sync_filter: Who sync lists. Empty: the user filter with * - everyone who can sign in.
fieldHints.sync_disable_missing: Accounts the directory made are switched off once it no longer lists them. Never an administrator or an account made here.
fieldHints.sync_groups: Every directory group becomes a filex group, kept in step. Which groups exist is managed on the directory.
fieldHints.sync_group_filter: Which directory groups to bring in. Empty: all of them - e.g. (&(objectClass=groupOfNames)(cn=dept-*)).
fieldHints.email_domains: Only these domains may sign in through it or get an account from it (e.g. partner.com). Empty: any.

upgradeHints.trust_email: The upgrade switched this on so that this provider works as it did before. Switch it off if the provider sends email_verified.

demo.title: filex - self-hosted file manager that embeds anywhere
demo.subtitle: One Go binary with a full web UI, pluggable storage/auth/DB drivers, live updates and presence, an embeddable web component, a desktop app whose folder sync is live, apps that add new things to do with a file, and a built-in MCP server so AI agents can drive it natively.

demo.alsoIncluded: Also included: apps - sandboxed WebAssembly add-ons installed through a permission review, with e-Signature, Convert, filextext and draw.io shipping alongside · language packs, right-to-left layout included · instance themes on the Appearance screen · the links you made, under My shares · personal and team tags · symlinked folders · a view and sort remembered per folder · roles, groups and per-person exceptions, per-file and per-folder access, and apps' own permissions · multi-tenancy, each tenant with its own sign-in realm and able to run itself - its own sign-in providers, domain and certificate · OIDC SSO, LDAP / Active Directory and sign-in with a Windows or Linux account · sign-in attempt limits with an IP allow-list · in-place viewers and editors, Office through ONLYOFFICE · thumbnails of SVG, HEIC, text and archives, and folders drawn with the files that came into them last · Default apps: which app opens a kind of file · creating a document from + New - Markdown, text, CSV and code anywhere, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OpenDocument wherever ONLYOFFICE is connected · a whole selection downloaded as one streamed archive · trash and versioning · replication · quotas · audit log · webhooks and in-app notifications · storage plugins · a persistent operation queue · a usage and cost view built from your storage provider's own daily report.

features.storageBody: Mount local disks, S3, SFTP, WebDAV, FTP/FTPS and SMB/NAS side by side as one tree - then reach that same tree back as S3, SFTP, FTPS, NFSv3 or WebDAV.
features.searchBody: Permission-aware full-text search across every storage. Try “budget 2026” for Documents/Budget-2026.csv, or “mian.go” - one typo forgiven - for Code/main.go. Tag a file, yours alone or shared with the team, and tag:yourlabel filters by it.
features.shareBody: Public links with a PIN, an expiry and a download limit, inbound drop links that collect files from other people - plus end-to-end encrypted folders the server cannot read.
features.desktopBody: The same explorer as a Windows, Linux or macOS app: several accounts at once, live two-way sync from the tray - an edit on either side arrives in about a second - a portable build on every platform for machines you may not install software on, and “filex mount” to attach a remote server as a Linux folder or a Windows drive.
features.embedBody: Drop the real file manager into your product as a Vue 3, React or framework-free web component, and hand AI agents a REST surface scoped by API key and a native MCP server.

A save to a file that already exists schedules one scan this many minutes later, and further saves inside that window join it rather than queueing more - so a burst of Ctrl+S costs one scan, and that scan reads the file's final state. The trade: a saved file can sit unscanned for up to this long after the last save.

loginSecurity.title: Sign-in security
loginSecurity.subtitle: Limits wrong password attempts at every door - the web form, WebDAV, FTP and SFTP - and shows who is locked out.

limit.title: Sign-in attempt limit
limit.desc: After this many wrong attempts inside the counting window, the account or the address is locked. Each new lock in a row lasts twice as long as the last, up to the longest lock.

allowlist.title: Allowed addresses
allowlist.desc: Addresses and networks that are never counted against the per-address limit, and may still sign in to a locked account - your office, your monitoring.

proxies.title: Trusted proxies
proxies.desc: filex believes the client address in X-Forwarded-For and X-Real-IP only when the request comes from one of these. A wrong list lets anyone claim any address, or makes every visitor look like your proxy.
proxies.addressesHint: A proxy that the switches above do not cover - on the host through a published port, on another machine, a CDN's edge in front of your own proxy: its address or network (CIDR).

class.autoHint: Worked out from where filex runs: this machine and, in a container, the container networks it is attached to - never their gateways, never the LAN.
class.loopbackHint: A proxy on the same machine as filex.
class.privateHint: The RFC 1918 and RFC 4193 private ranges: every machine on your LAN and every Docker network, gateways included.
class.linkLocalHint: Addresses a machine gives itself on a network segment.

proxies.trustsNobody: No proxy is trusted: the address a request comes from is always the client's own, and X-Forwarded-For is never read.
proxies.override: Saving stores this list here, and it takes precedence over the FILEX_TRUSTED_PROXIES environment variable. Remove the saved list to go back to the variable, or to the automatic default when the variable is empty.
proxies.resetConfirm: Remove the saved list of trusted proxies? The FILEX_TRUSTED_PROXIES environment variable, or the automatic default, is in force again.

auto.title: What automatic resolves to
auto.notInUse: Not in force: the list in force does not use it. Saving with this switch on puts it in force.
auto.excludedHint: Gateways and filex's own address: what the host relays (a published port's docker-proxy, a host process) or the container runtime relays (rootless Podman) arrives from them.

env.plain: filex runs directly on this machine, not in a container: only this machine is trusted. A proxy on another machine is named below.
env.container: filex runs in a container on a network of its own: the other containers on that network - a proxy container in front of filex - are trusted.
env.host-network: filex runs in a container with host networking: it sees the host's own network, so only this machine is trusted.
env.kubernetes: filex runs in a Kubernetes pod: the pod's own network is trusted. An ingress controller on another node is outside it - add your cluster's pod network (CIDR) below.
env.podman-rootless: filex runs in a rootless Podman container: its connections are relayed, so only this machine is trusted.
env.unknown: filex could not tell how it is connected, so only this machine is trusted.

reason.lan: on the LAN (macvlan or ipvlan) - not trusted
reason.tunnel: tunnel (user-mode networking or a VPN) - not trusted
reason.host: the host's own interface - not trusted

warning.unreadable: filex could not read how it is connected, so automatic trusts this machine only. Name your proxy below.
warning.ambiguous: What filex read about its network contradicts itself, so automatic trusts this machine only. Name your proxy below.

forwarders.title: A peer sends forwarded addresses and is not trusted
forwarders.desc: These sent X-Forwarded-For or X-Real-IP, but filex does not trust them: it ignored the header and counted every request as theirs. Is one of them your proxy? Trust it, and filex believes the client address it forwards.
forwarders.confirm:
Trust {address} as a proxy?

filex will believe the client address it forwards. If {address} is not your proxy, whoever sends from it chooses the address they are counted by: they can dodge the per-address limit or claim an address on the allow-list.
forwarders.confirmPublic: {address} is a public address. Trust it only if it is your own proxy or your CDN's edge, never a visitor's.
forwarders.confirmRelay: {address} is an address relayed connections arrive from - a container network's gateway, or filex's own address. Whatever the host or the container runtime relays arrives from it, a published port included. Trust it only when nothing but your proxy can reach that port (published on 127.0.0.1, or firewalled).

locks.title: Locks

appearance.previewHelp: Painted with the same theme variables the product uses, so this is what you get.
appearance.deleteConfirm: Delete the theme “{name}”? Anybody using it goes back to the default palette.
appearance.deleteFallbackNote: Deleting a theme puts everybody using it back on the default palette - nobody is left on a theme that no longer exists.
appearance.importBad: That file is not a filex theme.
appearance.contrastTitle: Some pairings are below the readability bar

pages.own: Colors of their own for the share and sign-in pages

css.warnTitle: Read this before you turn it on
css.warnScope: It never applies to the sign-in page or to this screen, so you can always get back here to switch it off.
css.warnNetwork: {'@'}import is stripped and every url() that is not a data: URI is made inert, so a stylesheet cannot call home.
css.warnLie: Within the screens it does reach, CSS can still hide, cover or relabel a control - including a delete confirmation. Only paste CSS you wrote.
css.warnOperator: Instance operators only. On a multi-tenant installation a tenant administrator cannot set this.

permissions.title: Roles
permissions.subtitle: A role is a named set of permissions. Everyone has exactly one - a built-in or a custom role, their own or given by a group they are in.

download.label: Download
download.hint: Save files and zips to a device; read them over WebDAV, SFTP, FTP, S3 or NFS. Previews stay open.

create.label: Add files and folders
create.hint: Upload, create folders and files, copy in, extract archives, restore from the trash.

modify.label: Change files
modify.hint: Overwrite, edit in the text editor or ONLYOFFICE, restore an older version.

rename.label: Rename
rename.hint: Give files and folders a new name in the same folder.

move.label: Move
move.hint: Move files and folders to another folder. Moving and renaming at once needs both.

delete.label: Delete
delete.hint: Move files and folders to the trash.

purge.label: Delete permanently
purge.hint: Empty the trash; delete on storages that have no trash.

encrypt.label: Encrypt
encrypt.hint: Create an end-to-end encrypted folder or file, or encrypt a folder you already have.

upload_links.label: Upload links
upload_links.hint: Create links other people can upload files through.

users.label: Share with people
users.hint: Give other accounts access to a file or folder.

use.label: AI agent API
use.hint: Let AI agents and MCP clients work with files through /api/ai.

run.label: Run apps
run.hint: Run app actions, such as signing flows.

webdav.label: WebDAV
webdav.hint: Connect over WebDAV, e.g. from the operating system’s file manager.

sftp.label: SFTP
sftp.hint: Connect over SFTP and register SSH keys.

s3.label: S3 access keys
s3.hint: Create S3 access keys and use them.

nfs.label: NFS exports
nfs.hint: Create NFS exports and mount them.

api.label: API keys
api.hint: Create personal API keys and use them.

desktop.label: Desktop app
desktop.hint: Sign in from the desktop app.

edit.label: Edit own profile
edit.hint: Change their own name, email, picture and password.

users.label: Manage users
users.hint: Users, their permissions, quotas and password resets - never an administrator's account.

grants.label: Manage folder access
grants.hint: See and remove every folder grant.

monitor.label: Monitor
monitor.hint: Dashboard, usage, sync history and the job queue, read-only.

full.label: Full administrator
full.hint: Everything else. Comes with the administrator role only.

source.role_off_group: role “{name}” from the group “{group}” is switched off

apps.hint: Permissions an installed app lets you give or take away, per role and per person.

holders.user: App default: people who can change files

apps.readOnly: Only an administrator can change app permissions.

card.title: Roles and permissions
card.subtitle: What this person may do: their role, and exceptions set for them alone. The result and where it comes from is shown beside each permission.
card.adminNote: Administrators hold every permission; roles and exceptions do not apply to them.
card.viewerNote: A read-only account can never add, change, delete or share files, whatever is set here.
card.conditional: Their role works differently in some folders; what is shown here applies everywhere else.
card.builtinRole: Role: {role} - change it in the account details above.
card.readOnlyRoleNote: “{role}” can only look at files, so adding, changing, deleting and sharing cannot be allowed as exceptions. Tick one of them in the role (or pick another role) to allow it.
card.groupRole: Role: {role}, through the group “{group}”. Their own role, picked above, would replace it.
card.groupReadOnlyNote: “{role}”, from the group “{group}”, can only look at files, so this account is a Viewer while it is in the group: its own Editor and Owner folder shares count as Viewer too.

rules.name: Role name
rules.builtinSummary: Its permissions are set from the row’s actions
rules.builtinPlatformOwned: The built-in roles belong to the whole platform and its operator manages them. For permissions of your own, create a role.
rules.viewerCeilingNote: A Viewer can never add, change, delete or share files; those stay off.
rules.ssoGroupsHint: A new account whose first sign-in carries one of these groups gets this role. After that, change it on the person’s page like anyone else’s.
rules.permissionsHint: Tick what people with this role may do. A new role starts from the Standard user preset; a preset replaces the ticks in one click.
rules.foldersHint: Optional. Pick storages or folders, then Allow or Deny file actions there. Everywhere else, the ticks above apply.
rules.disableConfirm: Switch off “{name}”? The {count} person holding it will have no access until it is switched back on. | Switch off “{name}”? The {count} people holding it will have no access until it is switched back on.
rules.deleteMove: {count} person holds this role. What should they have instead? | {count} people hold this role. What should they have instead?
rules.translations: Name and description in other languages
rules.translationsHint: Everyone sees the role in the language they use filex in. Where a language is left blank, they see the name and description above.
rules.deleteMoveGroups: Groups holding it: {count}. They get the role you pick, or none for User or Viewer.
rules.startingRoleLegacy: This only sets the role of a new account, once, at its first sign-in. For membership that follows the identity provider at every sign-in, link a group to the SSO group instead (Admin → Groups) and give the group this role.
rules.allThroughGroups: all through {count} group | all through {count} groups
rules.givenByGroups: given by {count} group | given by {count} groups

gaps.title: {count} role may have lost a permission | {count} roles may have lost a permission
gaps.why: It may have been dropped while the server ran an older version (0.50 or older) for a while; if it was taken away on purpose, dismiss this.
gaps.folders: {role}, in its folders: “{from}” is allowed, “{key}” is not.

twoFactor.title: Two-factor authentication required
twoFactor.body: Your administrator requires two-factor authentication for this account. Set it up to continue.

encryption.title: Encryption
encryption.subtitle: Choose who may create end-to-end encrypted folders and files here, and answer the requests waiting for your approval.

policy.title: Who may encrypt
policy.label: Policy
policy.unavailable: The platform operator has switched encryption off for your organization. You can still choose a policy; it takes effect when encryption is switched on again.

options.approval: Everyone whose role allows it, after an administrator’s approval

hints.off: Nobody can create a new encrypted folder or file. Existing ones keep working: they open, take new files and can be decrypted.
hints.admins: Only administrators may encrypt; everybody else is refused.
hints.permitted: Anyone whose role includes “Encrypt” in that folder (Roles). This is how filex has always worked.
hints.approval: As above, and anyone who is not an administrator needs an approval here first. Administrators are never asked. An approval is for one person, is used once, and opens only what was asked: one folder encrypted where it is, one new encrypted folder directly inside a folder, or one new encrypted file in a folder. It never reaches the folders below.

requests.title: Encryption requests
requests.subtitle: Under the approval policy, people ask here before they encrypt.
requests.expiresAfter: Unanswered requests and unused approvals lapse after {count} day. | Unanswered requests and unused approvals lapse after {count} days.
requests.loadFailed: The requests could not be loaded.

kind.folder: This folder, encrypted where it is
kind.newFolder: One new encrypted folder in this folder
kind.file: One new encrypted file in this folder

approve.title: Approve the request
approve.body: {who} may then encrypt {path} where it is. The approval can be used once, and not on a folder inside it.
approve.bodyNewFolder: {who} may then create one new encrypted folder directly inside {path}. The approval can be used once, and not on a folder that already holds something.
approve.bodyFile: {who} may then create one new encrypted file in {path}. The approval can be used once.

reject.title: Reject the request
reject.required: Write why - the requester is told.

requests.notPending: This request is no longer waiting: it was answered or it lapsed.

tenants.title: Tenants
tenants.subtitle: Switch encryption off for a tenant and nobody there - administrators included - can create encrypted folders or files. What is already encrypted keeps working.

groups.title: Groups
groups.subtitle: Named sets of people. Share a folder with a group like with a person, and give a group a role: everyone in it without a role of their own gets it. People join by hand here, or through an SSO or LDAP group their sign-in carries.
groups.deleteConfirm: Delete the group “{name}”? Its folder access goes with it. Its members keep their accounts, and anyone who had its role goes back to their built-in role.

fields.name: Name
fields.roleHint: Everyone in the group gets this role unless they have a role of their own.
fields.ssoHint: One per line, exactly as the sign-in carries it: an OIDC claim, an LDAP memberOf group, an operating-system group or a proxy header. People whose sign-in carries one join the group, and leave it when it stops.
fields.ssoAdminOnly: Only an administrator can link a group to SSO groups.
fields.priorityHint: For someone in several groups that give a role: the group with the highest priority decides (equal: the older group). A switched-off role is skipped for the next one.
fields.priorityAdminOnly: Only an administrator can change which group’s role wins.
fields.ldapHint: One per line: the group’s DN (cn=finance,ou=groups,dc=example,dc=com) or its name (finance), in any case. People whose LDAP sign-in shows the group join it, and leave it when it stops.
fields.ldapAdminOnly: Only an administrator can link a group to LDAP groups.
fields.adminHint: Everyone in the group is an administrator of filex. Linked to an LDAP group - named by its full DN, and counting only for people of that group’s own directory - the directory decides who: people who leave it lose administrator again (never the last administrator).

groups.addMember: Add a person by name or email…
groups.noMembers: Nobody is in this group yet.
groups.removeSsoConfirm: {name} is in this group through SSO. Remove them now? They join again at their next sign-in if the identity provider still puts them in it.

source.ssoHint: In the group through SSO - kept in step with the identity provider at each sign-in.

groups.foldersHint: Give the group a folder from the file explorer: Share → People, then pick the group like a person.
groups.noFolders: No folder is shared with this group yet.

userCard.title: Groups
userCard.roleFromGroup: With no role of their own, they have the role “{role}” through the group “{group}”.

groups.removeLdapConfirm: {name} is in this group through LDAP. Remove them now? They join again at their next sign-in if the directory still puts them in it.

directory.synced: Brought in by directory sync from the LDAP group “{name}”. Its members and its LDAP link follow the directory; its folders, role and priority are yours to set here. Which LDAP groups exist is managed on the directory.
directory.linkHint: Kept by directory sync on this group’s directory group.
directory.removedHint: Its LDAP group no longer exists: its LDAP members were taken out. Open it to delete it or keep it as a filex group.
directory.removedBody: The LDAP group “{name}” no longer exists in the directory, so its LDAP members were taken out of this group. Its folders, role and anyone added by hand are still here. Delete the group, or keep it as a filex group that no longer follows the directory. If the directory lists that same group again (for example after a filter change), this group follows it again; a group made anew there comes in as a new group.
directory.kept: This group no longer follows the directory.
directory.deleteNote: While the LDAP group exists, the next directory sync makes this group again - without its folders or role. To leave it out, remove it on the directory or narrow “Groups to bring in”.

accountHint.local: Made in filex: on this page, by an invitation or at setup.
accountHint.sso: Made by a sign-in through the SSO identity provider.
accountHint.ldap: Made by a sign-in through LDAP / Active Directory.
accountHint.proxy: Made by a sign-in through a trusted reverse proxy.

memberHint.manual: Added to the group by an administrator.
memberHint.sso: In the group through SSO - kept in step with the identity provider at each sign-in.
memberHint.ldap: In the group through LDAP - kept in step with the directory at each sign-in.

groupHint.local: Members are added by hand only.
groupHint.sso: Linked to SSO groups: members join and leave with the identity provider.
groupHint.ldap: Linked to LDAP groups: members join and leave with the directory.

tenants.title: Tenants
tenants.subtitle: Every tenant of this platform: its sign-in name (realm), its own address, the storages its people reach and its accounts. Only the platform operator manages tenants.
tenants.modeOff: Multi-tenant mode is off (FILEX_MULTI_TENANT): only the platform's own tenant can sign in. The other tenants and everything they have are kept, and their people sign in again when it is turned back on.
tenants.platformHint: The platform's own tenant: its people sign in with an empty realm, and its administrators administer every tenant.
tenants.oidcHint: The tenant's own identity provider, used on its own address. Empty: its people sign in with a password or through the platform's providers.
tenants.realmSuggestedHint: Suggested from the slug; you can change it now. Once the tenant is created it never changes: it is part of its people's addresses (alex{'@'}realm.local) and of the user names they save in their apps (realm/alex).
tenants.realmNewHint: Lower-case letters, digits and dashes. It never changes once the tenant is created.
tenants.realmLockedHint: The realm never changes: it is part of this tenant's account addresses (alex{'@'}{realm}.local) and of the user names its people saved in their apps ({realm}/alex). Changing it would cut both off.
tenants.platformRealmHint: The platform's own tenant has no realm: its people sign in with the Realm field left empty.
tenants.platformAlwaysOn: The platform's own tenant cannot be suspended.
tenants.platformNoDelete: The platform's own tenant cannot be deleted.
tenants.secretSet: Set (type a new one to replace it)
tenants.secretSetHint: Stored and never shown. Leave it empty to keep it.
tenants.storagesHint: The storages this tenant's people reach. A storage linked to no tenant is the platform's.
tenants.platformStoragesHint: The platform's own tenant reaches every storage; a link here only marks the storage as its own.
tenants.unlinkConfirm: Unlink {storage} from this tenant? The storage and its files stay; this tenant's people no longer reach it.
tenants.deleteConfirm: Delete the tenant “{name}”? Its storages are unlinked, never deleted, and their files stay.
tenants.deleteAccounts: Also delete its {count} account (its open links close) | Also delete its {count} accounts (their open links close)

fields.name: Name
fields.slugHint: A short name for the tenant, unique on this platform. The realm is suggested from it.
fields.slugEditHint: Changing it does not change the realm.
fields.enabledHint: Off suspends the tenant: none of its people can sign in. Nothing is deleted.
fields.hostHint: The host the tenant is reached at (files.acme.example). Its sign-in page names the tenant there, so its people type no realm. Empty: they sign in on the platform's address with their realm.
fields.cookieDomainHint: Shares the session across the tenant's subdomains (.acme.example). Empty: derived from the address. Set it when the address is a bare domain or its parent is a public suffix (.com.tr).
fields.adminGroupHint: People whose sign-in carries this group are the tenant's administrators.

errors.slug_taken: Another tenant already has this slug.
errors.host_taken: Another tenant already has this address.
errors.realm_invalid: Only lower-case letters, digits and dashes, at most 63, starting and ending with a letter or a digit.
errors.realm_taken: Another tenant already has this realm.
errors.realm_none: Nothing realm-shaped is left of this slug: type a realm.

tenantSelf.title: My tenant
tenantSelf.subtitle: Your tenant's own sign-in providers, the ones the platform gives it, and its own domains.
tenantSelf.signinHint: Your tenant's own OIDC or LDAP. Its people sign in through them with your realm; nobody else's people do.
tenantSelf.insecureHint: Off: this tenant's own providers may not reach a private or internal address, and an LDAP must use ldaps:// or StartTLS. On: both are allowed, for a directory inside your own network. Every change is in the audit log.
tenantSelf.insecureOn: The platform allows this tenant's providers to reach internal addresses and plain ldap://.
tenantSelf.guarded: Your providers reach public addresses only, and an LDAP is encrypted (ldaps:// or StartTLS).
tenantSelf.providerAdded: Provider added, switched off: fill it in, test it and switch it on.
tenantSelf.confirmFailed: Its test failed. Switch it on anyway?
tenantSelf.sharedHint: The platform operator decides which of the platform's providers serve your tenant.
tenantSelf.platformAddress: Your tenant's address on the platform:
tenantSelf.noTenantDomain: This installation gives tenants no address of their own, so a domain cannot be pointed at one (FILEX_TENANT_DOMAIN).
tenantSelf.domainsHint: To bring your own domain, create a CNAME record from it to {target}, then add it here. It works as soon as the record is seen, and stops working (until it is back) if the record goes. Use a name under your domain (files.acme.example): a bare domain cannot carry a CNAME.
tenantSelf.deleteDomainConfirm: Remove {domain} from this tenant? It stops working at once.
tenantSelf.ownCertificateSoon: Own, ends {when}: bring a new one
tenantSelf.acmeFailed: By filex (ACME): could not be obtained ({when})
tenantSelf.certificateHint: The certificate (with its chain) and its private key for {domain}, in PEM. The key is stored sealed and never shown again.
tenantSelf.ftpsNote: FTPS presents the server's one certificate: a client that checks the name refuses your domain on FTPS. SFTP and WebDAV are not affected.

why.no_cname: {domain} has address records of its own, not a CNAME to {target}
why.wildcard_cname: {target} is a CNAME to {found}: the platform's record for *.{tenant_domain} must be address records (A/AAAA)
why.dns_failed: The DNS could not be asked ({detail}); nothing was changed

domainErrors.domain_invalid: This is not a domain name a tenant can bring (a name with at least two labels, letters, digits and dashes).
domainErrors.domain_taken: This domain is already in use.
domainErrors.domain_reserved: This name is the platform's own.
domainErrors.no_tenant_domain: This installation gives tenants no address to point a domain at.
domainErrors.certificate_invalid: This is not a certificate and key in PEM.
domainErrors.certificate_key_mismatch: The private key does not belong to the certificate.
domainErrors.certificate_wrong_name: The certificate is not for this domain.
domainErrors.certificate_needs_secret_key: A private key is stored sealed, and this installation has no FILEX_SECRET_KEY.

appStore.title: Install from a store
appStore.subtitle: An app store sent you here with an install link. You read the review and decide; nothing is installed until you press Install.
appStore.none: There is no install link waiting. Open the store's Install link again.
appStore.reviewing: The review of {app} from {store} is open.
appStore.cancelled: Nothing was installed. The store was told that the link was cancelled.
appStore.declined: The store was not trusted and nothing was read from its link.

trust.newTitle: This store is not trusted yet
trust.newBody: filex accepts install links and license answers only from stores an administrator trusts. Before you trust this one, compare its key fingerprints below with the ones the store publishes on its own site.
trust.changedBody: The store now signs with keys that are not the ones it was trusted with. That happens when a store rotates its keys, and also when somebody else answers in its name. Compare the new fingerprints with what the store publishes before you trust it again.
trust.previous: The keys it was trusted with
trust.how: Only the keys listed here will be trusted. A key the store publishes later is asked about again.
trust.compared: I compared these fingerprints with what the store publishes and want to trust this store

wizard.title: Install {name} from a store
wizard.paidNote: This is a paid app. It is held (installed, running nothing) until the store confirms its license, and checked again every day.
wizard.keyFromStore: The store's link carries a license key ({prefix}). Leave the box empty to use it.
wizard.held: The app is installed but held: its license is {status}. Its page says why and takes a new key.
wizard.sourceOther: an upload or an address, without a store ({repo})

license.title: License
license.keySaved: The key was saved and checked.
license.heldNote: The app is held: its license is {status}. It stays installed with its settings and records, and runs nothing until the license holds again.
license.graceNote: The store could not be asked. The last valid answer holds until {until}.
license.storeUntrusted: {store} is no longer trusted here, so the license cannot be checked. Open an install link from that store to trust it again.

stores.title: Trusted stores
stores.intro: Install links and license answers are accepted only from these stores, signed with these keys. A store is trusted from its own install link.
stores.confirmRemove: Stop trusting {store}? Its install links will be refused, and the licenses it issued cannot be checked any more.

band.heldTitle: A paid app is held because its license does not hold
band.graceTitle: The store could not be asked about a paid app's license; it runs on its grace

err.store_invalid: That is not a store address filex talks to: a store is reached over https at a public address.
err.store_not_allowed: This server does not allow this store: FILEX_APP_STORE_URLS is set, so install links and licenses are taken only from the stores it lists (none, when it is empty), and no other store is trusted, not even on first use. The operator adds the store there.
err.store_key_not_configured: This store is configured on the server (FILEX_APP_STORE_URLS), but it signed with a key FILEX_APP_STORE_KEYS does not list. The operator adds the key.
err.store_unreachable: The store could not be reached. Try the link again in a moment.
err.store_bad_answer: The store answered something filex does not take: an answer it cannot read, a redirect (a store's API is asked without following one), or a time more than a day away from this server's clock - check the server's clock.
err.store_signature_invalid: The link's signature does not verify against the keys this store was trusted with. Nothing was installed.
err.intent_unknown: The store does not know this install link.
err.intent_gone: This install link was used already, or it has expired. Press Install in the store again.
err.intent_expired: This install link has expired. Press Install in the store again.
err.intent_used: This install link was already used on this filex.
err.intent_invalid: The install link is not one filex can act on: something a link must carry is missing or malformed (the filex it was made for, the commit, the manifest's hash). Press Install in the store again; if it happens again, the store's links need fixing.
err.intent_pin_mismatch: What the app's repository serves is not what the store approved ({fields}). Nothing was installed.
err.intent_pin_mismatch_commit: The release's tag no longer serves what the commit the store approved serves: the repository moved it ({fields}). Nothing was installed.
err.intent_wrong_instance: This install link was made for another filex ({link}); this one is {here}. Press Install in the store again and give it this filex's address.
err.intent_wrong_instance_public_url: This filex's FILEX_PUBLIC_URL is not an address store links can be held to (an http or https address with a host, and no user name, query or fragment), so no store link is taken until the operator fixes it.
err.store_source_changed: The installed version ({version}) came from {installed}; this link comes from {link}. A store link never moves an app to another store or repository, nor its license key. Remove the installed app first (that deletes its settings and what it kept), then open the link again.
err.store_source_changed_direct: The installed version ({version}) was installed straight from its repository ({repo}), not from a store. The paid link of {store} does not take an installed app under its license: to move to the store's paid version, remove the installed app first (that deletes its settings and what it kept), then open the link again.
err.intent_version_rollback: {installed} is installed; the link is for {link}, which is not newer. A store link installs or upgrades, never goes back.
err.intent_session_unknown: This review is no longer open: it was installed or closed already, or it timed out. Open the store's install link again.
err.license_key_invalid: That license key cannot be used: 4 to 512 characters, no spaces (and the server needs FILEX_SECRET_KEY to keep it).

appStore.malformed: This address is not a store's install link filex can read. Open the store's Install link again.
appStore.framed: A store's install link cannot be used inside a frame. Open it in its own browser tab.
